title: [v1] Advance the LR scheduler only after successful optimizer updates
head: 862ea673e01fafdb9ac9c6724f6e9d0c33f21d99
scope: Actual single-process SFTTrainer.fit with native GPT-2, tokenizer, renderer and batching; SGD/AdamW; NaN/Inf gradient injection, independent weighted-loss reference, full optimizer/scheduler state, disk checkpoint continuation.
peer_review: existing_prs reviewed exact full diff and native training tests; no blocker in scope.

dedup_review.notes: Actual related source/patches inspected. Legacy/KTransformers non-finite handling, FSDP synchronization, and scheduler initialization changes do not fix the v1 skipped-step schedule.

body:
## Problem

The v1 training loop skips `optimizer.step()` when the gradient norm is not finite, but still advances the learning-rate scheduler. A skipped update therefore consumes part of the schedule, so subsequent valid updates use the wrong learning rate.

## Change

Move `lr_scheduler.step()` into the successful-update branch, immediately after `optimizer.step()`. Gradient clearing still runs after every attempted update. The global batch/step counter and the DeepSpeed-managed path keep their existing behavior.

## Validation

[Native CPU before/after run](https://github.com/Afloat16/LlamaFactory/actions/runs/43418835563) for commit `862ea673e01fafdb9ac9c6724f6e9d0c33f21d99`, using PyTorch 2.9.1+cpu and Transformers 4.57.1:

- Baseline: 6 failures, 2 passing controls. Fixed: all 8 new cases pass.
- All 8 existing DPO precision and chunk-loss regression cases pass.
- Real `SFTTrainer.fit()` with a locally initialized GPT-2, actual tokenizer/rendering/batching, five update attempts, and two microbatches per attempt.
- SGD with momentum and AdamW, two parameter groups, clean training, first-step NaN, middle-step infinity, and consecutive non-finite updates.
- Gradient hooks inject non-finite values after the actual model backward. An independent explicit weighted-loss loop checks the learning rate used by every successful update, model parameters, optimizer state, and complete scheduler state.
- Saving and loading model/optimizer/scheduler state, followed by another real update, matches the reference continuation.
- Ruff check, Ruff format, and diff whitespace checks pass.

These are native single-process CPU training checks. The change is confined to the existing non-DeepSpeed update branch.
